audit.whatIsWrong: The level chart disagreed with the packet chart and with its own prose: rows 0-3 read Mordekaiser/Skill/Galio/Galio while whys[0] says level 1 is an even farm lane, whys[1] and phases[1].why say Q+W out-trade him, phases[2].why says 'the lane flips' your way, and whys[3] calls 4-5 a coin-flip. The packet levelChart is Skill/Mordekaiser/Mordekaiser/Skill.
audit.why: A 52.27% win rate over 49 games with a level-3 kit spike does not belong to Galio at levels 3-5, and the page rendered a side that contradicted the why-text sitting next to it.
audit.corrected: Rows 0-3 set to Skill / Mordekaiser / Mordekaiser / Skill in both layers, ratings adjusted to match, and phases[3].why rewritten so the Skill call is justified by Shield of Durand rather than reading as a Mordekaiser row.

audit.why: Spikes are stated correctly: level 2-3 (Q+W before he owns MR), level 6 Realm of Death, first item, and late-game MR stacking flipping the lane to Galio. Nothing to change.

audit.whatIsWrong: Justice Punch was described only as 'his dash + knockup engage' with no cooldown, so 'punish him when it's down' had no window attached. Shield of Durand's cooldown was never stated either.
audit.why: Justice Punch is 11/10/9/8/7 and is Galio's only dash — it is both his engage and his only exit, so a whiffed one is a full window. Shield of Durand is 18/17/16/15/14 and is the taunt that blanks your combo mid-trade.
audit.corrected: Real numbers written into dosFull[0].d, breakdown.cooldowns, whys[3] and phases[3].why so the advice keys to a concrete cooldown.
sources: enemyKit Galio E and W cooldowns

audit.why: The page already states the decisive interaction the mirror audit landed on: Hero's Entrance is global but worthless inside Realm of Death, and Justice Punch closes gaps rather than escaping. Both directions now say the same thing.
No verifiable patch movement for this pair on 26.15 from the data available; left alone rather than speculated.

edits.before: Q ranks make isolated hits massive. Galio must hug minions all lane; punish every step away from the wave with the full drag combo.
edits.after: Q ranks make isolated hits massive, but Shield of Durand blanks any trade you start into it — punish only his steps away from his wave.

edits.before: Through 4-5 it's a true coin-flip: you grind with the aura, but his Shield of Durand taunt can blank a trade outright if you mistime it.
edits.after: Through 4-5 it's a coin-flip: you grind with the aura, but Shield of Durand is an 18s taunt that blanks the whole trade if you eat the release.

edits.before: His dash + knockup engage. Punish him when it's down. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: Justice Punch is an 11-second dash-knockup at rank 1 — bait it, then run your pattern free.

edits.before: - Galio Justice Punch: matchup-defining — His dash + knockup engage. Punish him when it's down. Track it before every engage.
edits.after: - Justice Punch: 11s at rank 1 — his only gap-closer and his only way out. Spend E-pull and Q the second it whiffs.

notes: Both flagged suspectNames are false positives: 'Shield of Durand's' is the correct name with an English possessive, and 'Land Realm of Death' is the real name with a verb in front. No name changes made. Separately, the Mordekaiser kit file carries a derived flag on Q (Obliterate) reading 'grounding: shuts off enemy dashes' — Riot's own description of Obliterate says only that it smashes the ground for damage, increased against a single target. Mordekaiser has no grounding. Per the rule, I trusted the description and wrote nothing claiming Obliterate stops Justice Punch.
